rv.q: Silbiger's textured writing and Emily Moler's character-driven direction keep the proceedings from turning into flat liberal verses conservative discourse...
The puppet work of Twist remains dazzling, and each astonishing stage picture is more trippy than the last.
As dull as Very Blue Light can be, Silbiger is at least honest with how her characters end up, scattered to the winds and distracting one another with animated features on a Zoom call.
That it plays as well as it does is a tribute to Silbiger’s clever invocation of familiar themes, and a beguiling cast of four up-and-coming actors.

cn.t: Critics find this millennial coming-of-age drama thoughtfully captures contemporary political anxieties and generational limbo, though its pensive, talky nature and Chekhovian inertness leave some wanting more dramatic momentum.
